notes: Test genuinely pins the change: swapped internal/proxy/text2sql_handler.go for the origin/master version and ran TestExecuteReadOnlyQueryStatementTimeoutStopsSlowQueryOnDefaultDriver/driver=sqlite — FAIL after 30.02s (`slow query took 30.018s to fail (context deadline exceeded)`); on the PR tree PASS in 0.20s, with -race. Real modernc sqlite through the production executeReadOnlyQuery, no stubs. Tree restored, git status clean.

Ran: go build ./..., go vet, gofmt -l (clean), go test ./internal/proxy ./internal/config ./internal/text2sql -count=1 (all ok, proxy 59s). web: corepack pnpm install --frozen-lockfile, node --test scripts/run-tool.test.mjs 4/4 pass, `corepack pnpm run typecheck --silent` exit 0 (the runner's verify invocation).

Logic: execQueryDeadline(stmtTimeout) = stmtTimeout when 0<stmtTimeout<30s else 30s; negative/zero from admin_settings `adur` falls to the hard cap, so misconfiguration cannot remove the bound. Signature unchanged; all 4 callers (text2sql_handler.go:967, text2sql_scheduler.go:70, admin_text2sql.go:1639/1643) already pass StatementTimeout. pgx keeps SET LOCAL statement_timeout + work_mem.

Behaviour change to be aware of (not a defect): for pgx the client deadline now equals the server statement_timeout and starts before BeginTx, so on a runaway query the ctx usually fires first; pgx then closes that pooled connection instead of the server returning 57014 and keeping it. Both error texts contain 'deadline'/'timeout', so classifyText2SQLFailure (text2sql_handler.go:992) still reports 'timeout'. For MySQL only the client side is bounded — go-sql-driver closes the socket, the server statement runs until it notices; the docstring's 'bounded the same way as PostgreSQL' slightly overstates this. No live MySQL/PostgreSQL here; that part is by reading.

Docs drift, one-liner for a later round: README.md:892 still labels TEXT2SQL_STATEMENT_TIMEOUT '(postgres)' and README.md:855 describes the sandbox as postgres-only; docs/ADMIN_GUIDE.md:157 ('실행 제한') is still correct.

Scope: 6bbc8fc (web/scripts/run-tool.mjs, package.json scripts) is unrelated to the fix but is the same commit previously approved in the 09-17 and 09-19 runs and never rejected by the operator; it only affects how tsc/vite are invoked, has its own tests, and is needed for the runner's `pnpm run typecheck --silent` verify to pass. No dependency changes, no lockfile change.

Security/privacy: no new endpoints, no auth/session/migration files touched, no personal data, no new untrusted input — the only string interpolation in the function (work_mem) is pre-existing and admin-config-controlled. run-tool.mjs takes its package spec from package.json, not from user input. Fully revertible: no data or external state changes.
